## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uragajātaka* (Ja 154), translated as *The Snake*, is a birth story belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [Catalog]. According to the narrative framework recorded in the tradition, the Buddha recounted this discourse while residing at Jetavana to address a quarrel among soldiers, opening with the phrase "Concealed within a stone". In secondary scholarship, Cecil Bendall cites Jātaka No. 154 in his edition of Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya* as an instance demonstrating that serpents in Buddhist narrative literature are credited with the capacity for metamorphosis [Bendall 1902]. This text must be distinguished from the homonymous and widely known *Uragajātaka* of the *Pañcakanipāta* (Ja 354), which treats grief over a son's fatal snakebite [Bendall 1902].
